titulo: Train in a cycle: five, ten rounds and a list
lead: Once the agent can do the work, the part almost nobody does comes next: training. Don't ask just once. Ask five, ten times, evaluate it the way you'd evaluate an employee, gather the corrections into a list and run it in a cycle until it fixes everything. It takes more time and more usage, but in the end you have a written standard procedure that works for any agent.
objetivo: run the same task in a cycle, gather the corrections into one list, and close out a written standard procedure.

aprende.t: Why a single run fools you
From evaluation to the list of corrections

hero_alt: Humanoid robot at a table with five identical sheets in a row; a person points to the sheet marked with a red tag.

secoes.sub: Tap or click each step. The cycle only ends when the list is empty.

nos.detalhe: One good run can be luck; one bad run can be bad luck. Five to ten runs, with different inputs, show what the agent does every time and what it does only sometimes.
Look at all the results using the sheet's criteria and compare them with your example. Note for each run: "on task A I didn't like this, on B this was missing".
Put your notes together into a single list, with no repeats, from most serious to least serious. This is what you hand to the agent, not a pile of complaints.
Hand over the list, ask it to adjust, and run again. Cross off what passed, keep what failed. Repeat until the list is empty in every run.

With the list empty, ask the agent to write the standard procedure (a simple text): the steps, the rules that came out of the corrections, and the final test. It holds for the coming years and for any agent.

secoes.volta: Did any run fail? The failure goes back on the list and the cycle starts over
secoes.legenda: In my case (Nei, from INEMA), a good part of the day works like this: I delegate, I give feedback, and each correction becomes a written rule. In a way, I train the agent as much as it trains me.

rolagem_fim.texto: Run several times, evaluate, list, fix in a cycle until it is empty, and write the procedure. The same mistake doesn't come back.

texto: Each run in a new conversation of the same project: that way one run doesn't contaminate the other.
The list of corrections goes into the project instructions before the next run. A new conversation without the list in the instructions forgets everything.

exemplo.texto: Put the list in AGENTS.md (or in a file it points to), and make each round a new session.

texto: Use different cases in each round: an easy one, a hard one, a weird one.
Running the same case five times only measures luck.

exemplo.texto: A notice about a party, a schedule change and a bus strike.

texto: Also write down what turned out well: that is what goes into the procedure as "do it this way."
Without what worked, the list becomes just a list of bans.

exemplo.texto: Round 3: great opening, keep it. Missing the start date.

texto: Each line on the list says what to change in a way you can check.
"It felt off" doesn't help; "the date comes in the first sentence" does.

exemplo.texto: The start date appears in the first sentence.

texto: When a new model comes out, your employee gets smarter for free. Keep the list of tasks it does every time.
Run the procedure on the new model, compare quality and cost, and decide with the results in hand.

exemplo.texto: The same 5 inputs, on the current model and the new one, side by side.

secoes.sub: Copy and use. Replace the text between < > with your own.

blocos.conteudo:
# Evaluation · <task> · <date>
Criterion: the Measure from the sheet + the reference example

| round | input | passed the Measure? | what turned out good | what to fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | <case> | yes / no | | |
| 2 | | | | |
| 3 | | | | |
| 4 | | | | |
| 5 | | | | |

blocos.rot: Request: run again after pasting the list into the instructions
blocos.conteudo:
The list of fixes is in the project instructions, from most serious to least serious.
Do this task following the list: <this round's input>
When you finish, tell me which items on the list you checked and how.

abas.html:
1. The start date appears in the first sentence. (failed in 3 of 5)
  2. No student names, not even in examples. (failed in 1 of 5)
  3. The text fits on one phone screen. (failed in 2 of 5)

After the cycle: 5 of 5 on every item.

• One round and done: an error that shows up 1 time in 5 stays hidden until the day it matters.
  • A fix left loose in the chat: it disappears in the next conversation. It goes on the list and then into the procedure.
  • A procedure you write before the cycle: it comes from what the rounds showed, not from what you imagined.

secoes.sub: Use the sheet from lesson 4 and the goal from lesson 5.

exercicios.texto: Run the task from your sheet five times, each in a new project conversation and with a different input, and fill in the evaluation (document or spreadsheet).
exercicios.pronto: the table has five filled-in rows, with "yes" or "no" in the Measure column.

exercicios.texto: Gather what to fix into a single list, one checkable fix per line.
exercicios.pronto: the list has at least three fixes, and each one can be checked by looking at the result.

exercicios.texto: Paste the list into the project instructions, run the same inputs again (new chats), and repeat until they all pass.
exercicios.pronto: in one final round, all five inputs passed every item on the list.

exercicios.texto: Ask for the standard procedure and keep it with the sheet (in the chat, in the instructions or as a project file; in the terminal, in the folder).
exercicios.pronto: the file exists and has the rules that came out of the corrections and the final test.

secoes.sub: Train the agent like an employee.
The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Why run the same task five to ten times?
opcoes: To have more options and pick the best answer to hand in.
Because the agent learns on its own with each round and keeps getting better even if you give no feedback.
Because a single round can be luck or bad luck; several rounds show what it does every time.
perguntas.explica: An error that shows up 1 time in 5 only appears with several rounds. The agent does not learn on its own between them: what improves is the list you hand over.

perguntas.p: Which line works for the corrections list?
opcoes: The start date appears in the first sentence.
perguntas.explica: You can look at the result and check it. The others are opinion with no criterion: the agent doesn't know what to change.

perguntas.p: A new model came out. What is the right way to decide whether to switch?
opcoes: Run the procedure on the same inputs with both models and compare quality and cost.
Switch right away, because the new model is always better and cheaper than the previous one, for any task.
Wait for someone to comment on social media.
Rewrite all the prompts from scratch.
perguntas.explica: With the task list and the procedure saved, switching becomes a test: same inputs, side by side, quality and cost in hand.

itens.texto: Five to ten runs with different inputs show what the agent does every time.
Verifiable corrections, one per line, applied in a cycle until none are left.
The result of the training is a text that works for any agent and any new model.
